title: Factsheet: EU-wide guidelines on gender-neutral job evaluation and classification - Step-by-step toolkit
key_claim: The European Commission and EIGE have issued a practical step-by-step toolkit on gender-neutral job evaluation and classification to help employers comply with the EU Pay Transparency Directive; it is built around four objective and gender-neutral criteria (skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions) and updates the Commission's 2013 guidelines, with templates and methodologies calibrated to organisation size.
notes: EIGE publication factsheet, page metadata 'Publication date: 26 Mar 2026'; the updated guidelines were presented jointly with the European Commission in April 2026. EIGE is an EU agency (Tier 1). Verified via WebFetch; full page read.

title: Gender pay gap statistics (Statistics Explained, 2024 data)
key_claim: In 2024 the average unadjusted gender pay gap in the EU was 11.1% (gross hourly earnings), ranging from -0.8% in Luxembourg to 18.8% in Estonia; the gap is highest in financial and insurance activities (12.2%-40.3% across countries) and consistently higher in the private sector than the public sector, where transparent wage grids apply.
notes: Eurostat Statistics Explained living reference article; the page states 'Data extracted in February 2026' and 'Planned article update: February 2027' — treated as an evergreen statistical reference page, cited for 2024 reference-year data. Verified via WebFetch; full page read.

title: As pay transparency regulations come into force globally, only half of employers say they are prepared (2026 Global Pay Transparency Survey)
date_evidence: NEW YORK, February 16, 2026 ─ Mercer ... today released the results of its Global Pay Transparency Survey
key_claim: Mercer's 2026 Global Pay Transparency Survey (1,600+ multinational organisations across 60 markets, fielded September-October 2025) found employer preparedness rose to nearly 50% in 2025 from 32% in 2024, but only 14% have fully implemented their approach; only 9% of Europe-based employers say their transparency strategy is fully in place; disclosure of hiring pay ranges is expected to rise from 60% in 2024 to 94% by end-2026.
notes: Mercer press release, dated 'NEW YORK, February 16, 2026'. Tier 2 (major consultancy; disclosed methodology, real sample). 16 Feb 2026 falls in the 3-6 month band, so flagged is_structural_anchor: true (the canonical employer-readiness data source for this signal). Verified via WebFetch; full text read.

title: EU Pay Transparency: The Countdown Begins
date_evidence: meta-date: Mar 10, 2026 ... This Week in Leadership|March 10, 2026
key_claim: Korn Ferry analysis: the EU rules will force roughly 50,000 companies to increase pay and hiring disclosures; from 7 June 2026 employers must disclose a starting salary or range before first interview and may not ask candidates' pay history; firms 'will have to be able to defend their pay practices analytically, financially, and culturally', yet as of autumn 2025 only an estimated 16% of firms were prepared.
verbatim_quote: Companies anywhere in the world will have to be able to defend their pay practices analytically, financially, and culturally
notes: Korn Ferry 'This Week in Leadership' analysis, meta-date 'Mar 10, 2026', byline 'March 10, 2026'. Tier 2 (organisational/rewards consultancy). Verified via WebFetch; full text read.

title: First past the post: Slovakia becomes the first EU Member State to transpose the Pay Transparency Directive
key_claim: Slovakia's National Council adopted the Equal Pay Act on 15 April 2026, the first national transposition of the Pay Transparency Directive, entering force on the 7 June 2026 deadline; employers must have compliant pay structures in place by 31 July 2026; a joint pay assessment is required where an unjustified gender pay gap of 5% or more is identified; Slovakia gold-plates by extending equal-pay claims to same-sex comparators. One day after Slovakia's adoption, Estonia announced (16 April 2026) it would rather accept a fine than implement the Directive as drafted.
notes: Lewis Silkin employment-law insight, meta publishdate 2026-04-24. Tier 3 (specialist law firm analysis). Verified via WebFetch; full text read.

title: European Union: Transposition of the EU Pay Transparency Directive Across 27 Member States
key_claim: As of mid-April 2026 no EU Member State had fully completed nationwide transposition of Directive (EU) 2023/970: 4 had partial transposition in force (BE, CZ, MT, PL), 9 had published draft legislation, 13 had no public draft, and Sweden had publicly withdrawn its draft (26 March 2026), opposing the Directive and seeking renegotiation. Gold-plating is confirmed or signalled in 7 Member States; at least ten Member States are expected to face infringement proceedings for failure to transpose on time.
notes: L&E Global (international employment-law firm alliance) cross-jurisdiction transposition analysis, meta article:published_time 2026-04-20. Tier 3. Verified via WebFetch; full text and the 27-state table read. Primary source for the fragmentation evidence.

title: Pay transparency countdown: Is Europe ready for the 2026 equal pay test?
date_evidence: euronews.com/business/2026/03/03/pay-transparency-countdown-is-europe-ready-for-the-2026-equal-pay-test  (headline: Pay transparency countdown: Is Europe ready for the 2026 equal pay test?)
key_claim: With EU countries due to incorporate the Pay Transparency Directive by early June 2026, Europe is widely seen as unprepared: as of January 2026, nine of 27 countries had taken no action toward implementing the directive, and Mercer's survey found only 9% of Europe-based employers had a full transparency strategy.
notes: Euronews Business article, publication date 3 March 2026 (from URL path and confirmed in headline/dateline). Tier 3 (quality journalism). Verified via WebFetch; article body read from the saved response. Reports the Addleshaw Goddard tracker and Mercer survey figures.
